Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Swelling of the left elbow for approximately one week, noticed incidentally in the shower.
- Symptoms: Swelling is not painful, slightly warm, sensation of fluid present. No significant tenderness; feels "weird" but not limiting movement.
- No history of trauma or injury to elbow.
- Denies previous similar episodes.
- No significant physical activity at work (desk job).
- Past medical history: Osteoarthritis (diagnosed by GP a few years ago).
- Allergies: Peanuts.
- No known medication allergies.
- Medications: None regularly.
- Social history: Regular runner (2–3 times weekly), healthy, mobile, active.
- No history or family history of rheumatologic disease (e.g., rheumatoid arthritis, lupus).
- No personal or family history of eczema.
- Reports isolated dry skin on the tip of the affected elbow; denies dry skin elsewhere.

Objective:
- Left elbow: Visible swelling, slightly warm to touch compared to adjacent skin.
- Mild discomfort on palpation next to swelling, but not overtly tender at tip.
- Full range of motion preserved; patient able to move elbow normally.
- Skin at the tip of the elbow appears mildly dry.
- No suggestion of systemic illness (no systemic symptoms reported).
- No signs of septic arthritis or acutely infected joint as per virtual examination.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Left Elbow Swelling
   - Assessment: Probable left olecranon bursitis.
   - Differential diagnosis: Gout, infection (septic bursitis), inflammatory arthritis.
   - Investigations: Blood tests to check inflammatory markers, infection, rheumatological antibodies, and gout screen (to be performed at patient's convenience with forms sent by mail).
   - Treatment: Start ibuprofen 400 mg twice daily after food (over-the-counter).
   - Follow-up: Arrange follow-up visit (in-person, video, or phone as preferred) after blood test results (~1 week). Advise to contact clinic promptly if elbow becomes very red, increasingly painful, or if redness spreads (to rule out septic arthritis/emergency).

Quality checks:
●	Missing information: No medication reconciliation beyond current statement ("none"), no specific review of systems for fever/chills, no documentation of baseline vitals, dosing instructions provided for ibuprofen but not documented as clear prescription.
●	No internal conflicts noted.
●	Transcript quality: Clear, some repetitive conversational elements, but all clinically relevant information present.
